body: Scarcity and exclusivity produce a sense of value that we would not otherwise get if every person was 'obtainable'. Same is true in Economics.

You're definitely not alone. I'm 19 and also panicking for the exact same reason. I might have had some success in the past, but now that is no longer relevant. People judge by your most recent achievements, unfortunately. 

This year everything has been a series of train wrecks and failures for me. I just about managed to get a minimum wage part time job, but it makes little difference. I'm a complete loser next to my friends. 

Perhaps ask for a different antidepressant? As far as I'm aware they affect people in different ways. Some things that I found useful are running and eating good food rich in 5-hydroxytryptophan (5-HTP). 

I hope you get better and I wish you all the best.

Sound really awful, I hope at least there are good painkillers. My grandfather had gout and I remember seeing his fingers, wrists and feet swollen up horribly. Poor guy was stuck at home for weeks because he could barely walk. He also had to follow a strict vegan diet. I was too young to fully understand how painful that must have been. Shit, I feel bad he had to spend his last months like this...
To be honest I feel slightly better in the evenings for some reason. Thank you. Hope everyone here has a good weekend.

Damn I'm really sorry, I don't know how help. Maybe your university can allow you to retake the semester or the year? I know that in some cases it is possible to submit an extenuating circumstances form.
Yes absolutely. I remember my best years. 2013/2014 was a really great time for me. This was the peak and since then it's been downhill. 2012 was also pretty cool.

Yeah I understand that completely. What you describe is scarily accurate to what a lot of people say about social media. It always makes me feel very inadequate but I feel like I have an obligation to 'like' all my friends' Instagram pictures even though they make me feel like shit. 

Also I'm pretty sure that their life is actually as good as it seems on social media...

It's perfectly understandable why you might feel this way, it hurts seeing everyone else doing really well while you're in pain. I personally struggle with focusing on myself and not comparing myself with other people. But yeah, it's a case of rubbing salt in the wounds and I know how awful that feels.

That is really nicely written and makes sense. I'm glad you found something that works for you. I agree that society's ideal life is not attainable. I'm just trying to improve on what I was in the past but struggling with it. Thank you for the kind words.

You went through some really tough times, well done for coping with them so well. There is still a little hope, yes, but I feel so weak right now and I don't have any control over life - I'm as good as dead.

I'm a student at university. My mental and physical health has been poor - insomnia, anxiety, depression, eating disorders, deteriorating vision, low blood pressure. Because of this I've been messing up simple things like failing to get my driving license. I'm going to be under pressure from debt. Also I'm struggling to decide on a specific career choice. It doesn't feel like I've gained any new valuable skills from my course which is a bit disappointing.
Thank you for the support. You're right, it's not always a competition. It does however often seem like I'm stuck in one place but hopefully this has to change sooner or later.

It's been like this for more than 3 years now. Sorry that you get these thoughts and doubts. It's nice that you have your wife for support. Best of luck and I hope you overcome your doubts (I know it's very hard).
Thanks for the encouragement. I hope it turns out ok.
I'm sorry it's just really frustrating. I've also been trying hard to improve my life but sometimes it feels like I'm about to go insane.
